title: Bills Place 26-Year-Old WR on PUP to Open Training Camp
description: The Buffalo Bills placed a 26-year-old wide receiver on their PUP list as training camp opened up on Tuesday. The post Bills Place 26-Year-Old WR on PUP to Open Training Camp appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Buffalo Bills veterans reported to training camp on Tuesday, which means football is finally here! However, it also means that it’s almost time for the team to make critical roster moves to get everything ready for the regular season in September.

The Bills still have a few more weeks before they need to start making major roster decisions, but they did make one on Tuesday with wide receiver Tyrell Shavers. Buffalo placed him on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Shavers tore his ACL in the Bills’ wild-card win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in January. It’s only been six months since Shavers’ injury, and usually ACLs take nine months to a full year to come back from.

Since Shavers is on the PUP list, he can participate in all team activities except for practices until he is activated. If he remains on the PUP list by the time the Bills reduce their roster to 53 players, he will have to miss at least four games in the regular season.

The 26-year-old receiver played in all 17 games for the Bills last season, recording 15 receptions for 245 yards and one touchdown. Even though Shavers didn’t have the most productive performance during the regular season, he was a fan favorite in the preseason last year.

In three preseason games, Shavers recorded six receptions for 123 yards and one touchdown, which caused many fans to become attached to him.

Hopefully, Shavers will return from his injury this season, giving the Bills a boost toward the playoffs.

title: Jerry Jones opens Dallas Cowboys training camp with drama, willing to make trade to bolster Super Bowl chances
description: Leave it to owner Jerry Jones to add a little spark to what had been a largely quiet offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, even while admitting he planned to do...
fullText:
Leave it to owner Jerry Jones to add a little spark to what had been a largely quiet offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, even while admitting he planned to do no such thing.

Jones simply can’t help himself.

Of course, things started normally at the press conference on Tuesday to open Cowboys training camp for the 2026 season in Oxnard, Calif..

Jones initially, made fun of the idea that the Cowboys had a quiet offseason, considering all the moves they made with the coaching staff, hiring nine new assistants, led by defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

And Jones, who admitted last year that when things are quiet around the Cowboys he would often do something to stir the pot, played along with the perception.

“I’ve never thought that there was anything quiet or subdued about the Dallas Cowboys,” Jones said. “I’ve never thought of it that way, but I have been guilty of stirring it up. And you guys help me. And we have been a great team. I promise you that for the last 30 something years. And so that does happen and it is good. I do like the perception that we’ve had a quiet uneventful off season and let’s see how we can work in that. Perception is big. Perception is big. But what I will tell you is I don’t plan on doing anything around here for the next few days to stir anything up.”

It certainly helped that there was no contract drama with receiver George Pickens, who signed his franchise tag and joined the team for camp with no plans of a hold out.

“I personally like the fact that the perception is that it’s been a quiet, non-confrontational off season,” Jones said. “That’s good. I have really a lot of that where I live in my mind. I do, but I have some times when it’s not fun too. So all that’s good. I like the mood.”

And yet, a few minutes later when asked about Super Bowl chances, Jones bolstered quarterback Dak Prescott’s Super Bowl or bust mantra for 2026 by adding his own drama to proceedings with a promise to add a difference-making player to make it happen.

He said he feels that good about his team and their hopes of ending what is now a 31-year drought since their last Super Bowl title following the 1995 season.

“I’d give up future to add substantive to where we are today as to a player, to give you an idea about would I invest something substantive to get the right kind of deal to improve us opening day. I would,” Jones said. “I feel that good about this team this year.”

Jones then doubled down on his comments by saying he talked to a owner on Monday about making a “substantive” trade.

“I think we’ve got a chance to be worthy of spending some future if we saw an opportunity,” Jones said. “Those kinds of conversations that are ongoing…I talked about a situation yesterday with another team and another owner. Yesterday.”

Jones comments only opened the door to widespread speculation on which owner he talked to and which player he was talking about.

It also spawned a question about the failed trade attempt for Las Vegas Raiders defensive Maxx Crosby in March and whether it could be back in play.

Crosby was initially dealt to the Baltimore Ravens, who then backed out the deal because of injury concerns.

Jones still acknowledges that one of the key areas they could bolster a difference-making player is edge rusher/defensive end.

Why did you walk away from Max Crosby when it fell apart with the Ravens and not revisit that then?

Can you elaborate on that for me?

“No, because there’s nothing more to elaborate about, but we did not walk away,” Jones said. “That’s about all there is to say, but we understood his injury well. And so we thought he could help us then. And we’re surprised the way that was resolved. But to basically take what happened with him after he came home back to the Raiders, to inject anything about what we’re thinking or doing and because he went back to the Raiders would be a mistake.”

Vice president Stephen Jones had to chime in and let Jerry Jones know that because Crosby is still with the Raiders he is getting close to tampering by continuing the conversation.

When asked in general of Crosby was the type of difference-making player he was looking to add, Jones responded in kind.

“Let’s don’t hypothetical here…That is tampering,” Jones said. “It really is. And so we don’t want to talk like that and act like that. But that is a good example of what you can stand ready for if in fact you think the rest of your team is coming along well, then those things stay alive. It is a good indicator of how good we feel about the team, the fact that we could do things like you’re talking about right there. I’ve really got to emphasize here he is a Raider. He’s a complete Raider, a happy Raider, everything in the book. And we shouldn’t even be having this kind of discussion with him.”

Now regarding the discussions with the other owner, there is nothing imminent on the horizon, Jones said No trade is afoot for the Cowboys.

But he is ready and willing to do something to light a fire under the Cowboys’ Super Bowl chances after what has been a “quiet” offseason.

Prescott has said as much and embodied the team’s goal by arriving to training camp with Super Bowl t-shirt on.

“That’s always been my mindset. It’s the one thing I truly love about the Cowboys organization and the fanbase is it’s that or nothing,” Prescott said recently. “As I said wherever that was, that’s what being a competitor is. If that’s not how you’re wired, if that’s not how you think, whether you’re a fan, whether you’re a player, whether you’re a coach, then I think you’re in the wrong business and honestly I don’t want you on my team. I love those expectations and they’ll always be there.”

“Dak’s feeling about it is more important than me feeling about it because Dak actually tangibly can cause his teammates to play at a higher level than I can,” Jones said. “So when Dak is that positive about it, that adds some credibility to it. I too can say that the fact that Dak is looking at what he’s looking at causes me to feel the same way. I think we’ve got a chance to really be good. I love the excitement.”

“You guys don’t expect us to be a contender in the Super Bowl,” Jones added while pointing to the media. Y’all don’t? Why would you? I like that. I do. I like that. And I like what we put together to show you that we can do it.”

He also plans to add to it, if necessary to make it happen.

Just don’t ask about Maxx Crosby.

title: It's not just triple-digit velocity. Jacob Misiorowski might be throwing the best fastball in baseball history
description: Jacob Misiorowski is regularly throwing 100 mph or more. That's only part of the reason for his success.
fullText:
We can say it now: Jacob Misiorowski is probably going to win the NL Cy Young Award this year, barring an injury or “Space Jam”-esque draining of talent. Anyone who looks at the stats can tell you that. Anyone who looks at the odds in Vegas can tell you that. And anyone who watched the Milwaukee Brewers ace's latest start can probably tell you that.

Misiorowski's 12-strikeout performance against the Colorado Rockies in Milwaukee is best described as one-half of the greatest start in MLB history. He struck out the first seven batters he faced and retired every batter until there were two outs in the fifth inning, at which point Cole Carrigg ended the perfect game and shutout bid with a home run. Chad Patrick was on the mound for Milwaukee when the sixth inning began.

Obviously, it's easier to dominate for four-and-a-half innings than nine innings, but the thing is, Misiorowski has already done the latter this season, too. Facing one of MLB's better offenses in the Philadelphia Phillies, the flame-thrower faced the minimum in a one-hit, 15-strikeout shutout on June 12.

Through 120 innings this season, Misiorowski has been so good that if he posted a league-average ERA (4.21) for the remaining 42 innings he needs to qualify for the ERA title, he would still rank second in the NL in ERA and third in MLB overall.

It's actually not that common for the hardest-throwing starter in MLB to also be the best starter in MLB, but Misiorowski appears to have reached that plane of dominance. And it's not just that he throws triple-digit heat.

It can be argued that this guy is throwing the best fastball in the history of the sport when it comes to everything we use to evaluate pitchers.

OK, we need to throw out some qualifiers here. The words "best" or "greatest" can mean so many things, hence why GOAT arguments are interminable across sports. It could mean success relative to your peers, but for our purposes, we're talking about a 1-to-1 comparison level, regardless of era.

So with apologies to quite a few pitchers, we're going to invoke the Adam Ottavino Principle. That refers to when a very good reliever confidently stated he could strike out Babe Ruth because baseball has never been played at a higher level than it is today when it comes to pure stuff. The pitchers have never thrown harder, and if you were to take a league-average pitcher in 2026 and send him back to the 1920s or maybe even the 1970s, the result would likely be carnage against that era's batters. It takes years of experience to catch up to a 100-mph fastball, and the only way to do it is to regularly face that level of velocity.

There have obviously been hard throwers in the past, such as Bob Feller and Nolan Ryan. Misiorowski throws harder than them (though no one is saying they couldn't match him if given access to modern training and techniques).

As MLB.com's Mike Petriello broke down, there are stories of those guys and others getting measured well past 100 mph, but so much of that mythology is built on single pitches outside of elite competition and a fervent belief that certain radar guns were accurate while producing outlier numbers. Simply hitting 100 mph was a milestone in the 20th century, and it's basically impossible that any starting pitcher from the days before modern pitch tracking hit 100 mph as regularly as Misiorowski does.

This season, the right-hander has hit triple digits on 42.1% of his four-seam fastballs, per Baseball Savant, and the only other starting pitchers who have reached double digits in that stat are the famously hard-throwing Hunter Green (16.9% in 2025) and Jacob deGrom (15.1% in 2023).

Misiorowski is the apex predator of pitch velocity, but that's not the only reason we’re saying his fastball is better than any other in history. We can hear the coaches (and Mike Rizzo) already, saying that fastballs are more than velocity. They're about placement. They're about trajectory. They're about movement.

Misiorowski rates from good to elite on all of those, too.

For starters, let's talk about extension. Releasing the ball closer to the plate than the average pitcher has the same effect as adding speed to your fastball: It gives the batter less time to react. At 6-foot-7, Misiorowski releases the ball as close to the plate as anyone, and that's why he's so comically far ahead of the pack in a stat called perceived velocity, which factors in extension to figure out which pitches go from the pitcher's hand to the strike zone the quickest.

Among starting pitchers in the pitch tracking era, Misiorowski is the all-time leader in fastballs with a perceived speed of at least 103 mph, with 710. Second-most is Jordan Hicks with … six.

There are relievers who have posted hundreds of such pitches, such as Aroldis Chapman (673) and Mason Miller (260), but none of them matches the rate that Misiorowski throws them. And it needs to be said: None of those guys does his thing for more than an inning or two. In that shutout against the Phillies, Misiorowski hit 103.4 mph on his first pitch and 103.1 mph on his final pitch.

Combine that extension with a low arm angle, and you have a pitch designed to fly through the easy-power, uppercut swings that define this era.

As for movement, Misiorowski's four-seamer is third in spin rate in MLB this season. The actual movement doesn't rank as high because the ball has so little time to move, but it definitely has life.

As for control, let's take a look at a Statcast leaderboard that measures the rate at which pitchers land their four-seamers and sinkers in the zone. Misiorowski ranks 45th out of 401 pitchers with at least 100 such pitches this season. Take away the middle-middle part of the zone (i.e. the meatballs), and he ranks 36th.

103.4 MPH Fastball
103.2 MPH Fastball

91.3 MPH Curveball
104.5 MPH Fastball
104.1 MPH Fastball
103 MPH Fastball

Jacob Misiorowski struck out the first 7 batters with pure heat 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/5neQFMra9M

That is admittedly a lot of numbers, so here's the summary: This is a pitcher who almost certainly throws harder than any pitcher in history, releases the ball as close to the plate as anyone, spins the ball as much as anyone and hits the good parts of the strike zone at a well-above-average rate.

It's everything you could possibly want in a fastball, and the results line up with the peripherals.

Remember that start against the Rockies? Misiorowski got swinging strikes on 23 of 41 swings against his four-seamer, an absurd 56% whiff rate. He did that against a team that currently ranks fifth in MLB in wOBA against pitches 98 mph or faster outside of Coors Field.

As far as this season goes, Misiorowski leads all starting pitchers with a 42.6% whiff rate on his four-seamer. As far as overall results go, only Cleveland Guardians rookie Parker Messick matches Misiorowski in xwOBA, which uses batted-ball data to estimate how much success batters deserve on a given pitch. Unlike Messick, Misiorowski doesn't back up his fastball with a changeup used on a quarter of his pitches.

There have been other freak fastballs in history. Walter Johnson and Randy Johnson both threw elite velocities in their eras, from a place no batters were used to seeing the ball. The real key to a great fastball, or any pitch, is for it to do something the batter is not used to. And Misiorowski certainly does that in a way no other pitcher can replicate across history.

Misiorowski is in Year 2. Many of the legends we have or could compare him to maintained their level for a lot longer. We are merely saying that, right now, Misiorowski is throwing his fastball at a level we've never before seen in baseball.

A lot could change in the years to come. Throwing a 103 mph fastball requires a kinetic chain so violent and complicated that this level could very well be fleeting. Every successful career requires adjustment, to both the league's changes and your own body's changes. Misiorowski would be a very different pitcher if he sat at 97 mph, and that might be a form we see someday.

That's to say nothing of the injury risk. Major surgeries are inevitable in modern pitching, especially among starters who live in the upper-90s and above. The list of pitchers in that group who have blown out is considerable: Greene, deGrom, Noah Syndergaard, Spencer Strider, Stephen Strasburg, Eury Perez, Shohei Ohtani, Gerrit Cole, Sandy Alcantara, Matt Harvey and many more.

It's honestly not a helpful question to ask whether Misiorowski will stay healthy. He almost certainly won’t. The relevant question is whether he will be able to come back and still dominate.

We don't know what will happen in the future for Misiorowski or any pitcher. It's the price of playing the game that Misiorowski is helping to define right now — but that doesn't mean we can't enjoy what's currently in front of us.

description: Rodgers is ready to call it a career.

Football fans hoping that Aaron Rodgers might decide to continue his career beyond the 2026 NFL season are going to be disappointed.

At the onset of Pittsburgh Steelers training camp, Rodgers made it clear that the '26 season will absolutely be his final run. "Zero debate," he said, via ESPN.

Rodgers, 42, explained that he fully believed that the 2025 season would be his last, but Pittsburgh's decision to hire Mike McCarthy as head coach led to Rodgers returning for one final season. Rodgers and McCarthy enjoyed some serious success together as the quarterback and coach duo in Green Bay for over a decade.

"I thought last year might be it," Rodgers said. "And then Mike [McCarthy] got hired, and I talked to the wife and she said, 'You can do one more year.' I said, 'Well, we'll see if it works out.' And then it kind of all came together."

So, football fans should appreciate watching Rodgers while they can during the upcoming season, because it will be a wrap after that.

title: Record-setting Sandy Alcantara aces Phillies to push Marlins to .500
description: Sandy Alcantara dazed deadwood swingers with lethal pitches, carrying the Miami Marlins to victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Tuesday in Miami.
fullText:
MIAMI, July 28 (UPI) -- Sandy Alcantara dazed deadwood swingers with lethal pitches, carrying the Miami Marlins to victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Tuesday in Miami.

With the 1-0 triumph, the Marlins (54-54) climbed back to .500 and earned their second consecutive victory after snapping a franchise-record dozen-game losing streak Monday at loanDepot park.

Alcantara allowed just four hits over seven scoreless innings. The Cy Young Award-winning ace also set a franchise record with the 111th quality start of his decorated MLB career.

The Marlins jumped on the scoreboard first when first baseman Kyle Stowers crushed a hanging knuckle curve to right center for a 390-foot solo homer in the first inning. That proved to be the only run needed as Alcantara, who didn't allow a hit until the fifth, kept the Phillies quiet for the majority of the night.

He hurled seven different pitches against Bryce Harper and the Phillies' talented lineup, keeping them off balance with his sinker, cutter and rare curveballs.

Is it? Is it? IT IS. pic.twitter.com/qKYg8jv1c1— Miami Marlins (@Marlins) July 28, 2026

Marlins relief pitchers Calvin Faucher and Pete Fairbanks did not allow a hit, run or walk over the final two innings to preserve Alcantara's gem.

Designated hitter Liam Hicks went 2 for 4 in the victory. Second baseman Xavier Edwards, who went 1 for 2 with two walks, was the only player to reach base more than twice in the matchup.

Phillies starter Aaron Nola allowed five hits over 5 2/3 innings. His lone blemish was Stowers' solo shot. Right fielder Bryan De La Cruz, who went 2 for 3, was the only Phillies player with multiple hits.

With Tuesday's win, the Marlins also earned their 16th series victory over the season. They've now won or tied 18 of the 35 series they've played this season. They entered Tuesday with four consecutive series losses.

The Phillies (57-51) loss was their sixth in seven games. They remain in second place in the National League East, six games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (62-44).

The Marlins, who sit in fourth place in the National League East, will host the Phillies in the series finale at 12:10 p.m. EDT Wednesday in Miami.

title: Jets QB Geno Smith moving forward, hates that offseason dispute with ex-girlfriend was a ‘distraction’
description: Geno Smith was investigated by Florida police after an incident with an ex-girlfriend earlier this summer, though he was not arrested or charged.
fullText:
Geno Smith is trying to move on and focus on football after he was involved in a domestic incident with a former girlfriend at his Florida home last month.

The New York Jets quarterback was not arrested or charged after the incident, which took off on social media earlier this offseason. Smith revealed on Tuesday that he has since discussed the matter with head coach Aaron Glenn, general manager Darren Mougey and other veterans on the team.

“I really hate the fact that something I was part of could’ve been a distraction for this team, my teammates and this organization because a lot of hard work has been put in,” Smith said, via ESPN. "A lot of guys have put in a lot of work for us to be in a good spot as a team. I'm happy that I'm able to put this behind me. I'm looking forward to moving forward."

The investigation started after an incident on June 21 in which a woman who said she was Smith’s ex-girlfriend posted a video on social media and called 911 accusing Smith of assaulting her. She told a 911 dispatcher that “my ex-boyfriend just beat me up,” and that it was caught on camera.

She also posted a video on social media with the caption: “Geno Smith beat my ass cause he hates taking care of his special needs kid and can’t be left alone with him.” That video showed her following Smith around his home yelling at him, but did not show any evidence of an assault.

Smith was never arrested, and the woman was trespassed from his property. Smith had two scratches on his face and a knot on the back of his head, and the woman had a small cut along the webbing of her right hand and a bruise on her left arm.

That led to an investigation into Smith, though it was closed earlier this month. Smith will not face charges. Police cited the absence of witnesses and surveillance footage to corroborate the allegation. Smith also reportedly provided police with Ring camera footage that “did not show any physical altercation.”

Smith, who was dealt to the Jets in March in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, did not get into what he said to his teammates or the Jets staff.

“We have a tight brotherhood in this locker room,” linebacker Demario Davis said, via ESPN, while confirming that he spoke with Smith about the incident.

"Nobody is operating in a silo on this team, and we need that. People need space where they can have people they know and trust that will protect them the right way."

Smith, who got his start in the league with the Jets back in 2013, is entering his 13th season in the league this fall. He threw for 3,025 yards and 19 touchdowns and 17 interceptions with the Raiders. Smith will attempt to lead the Jets, who went just 3-14 last season, to the playoffs for the first time since the 2010 campaign.

title: Daniel Rodriguez enters UFC Belgrade with new perspective after prison time
description: UFC headliner Daniel Rodriguez spent much of the past year in a Mexican prison, and couldn't be happier with how things have turned around.
fullText:
A few months ago, Daniel Rodriguez would not have fathomed he'd be headlining a UFC event in Belgrade, Serbia, to kick off the promotion's August schedule.

But fight week is underway, and Rodriguez (20-5 MMA, 10-4 UFC) is across the pond, soaking in the moment despite its business trip elements. More than anything else, he's just happy to be free.

"It's a dream come true," Rodriguez recently told MMA Junkie. "It's stuff you dream about while I was sitting in the jail cell. To get out and for all the positive things that have happened since, it's just amazing. It's really unbelievable."

Rodriguez, 39, spent eight months in a Mexican prison after being arrested with marijuana on his person as he crossed the border. While he was able to train and work out, Rodriguez admits that it took him a while to truly get back in "MMA shape."

"Getting released from prison, I thought I was in shape until I started doing some of the stuff you normally do during training," Rodriguez said. "It was definitely a process getting my body back to being able to perform at an elite level. It was all part of the process. I just had to trust the process and embrace the journey. I believed in the work I had ahead of me. I was a little discouraged at first. But with a situation like this, headlining a UFC event, made me realize this was real.

"I'm very grateful to still be able to do this because there was a moment in time where I didn't think I was going to be able to continue my career. Now that I'm able to, it definitely brings it to a new light in my life. I can say the difference in this fight camp is I've been a lot more dedicated and focused than my other fight camps. I've just been really playing this one out right and show up to practice every single day, show up to the gym every single day. I've barely taken days off, only when the coaches made me take days off. Even when they did, I would still go for a long-ass run or still do my own thing."

Though the process was a bit harder and longer, Rodriguez thinks he can pick up where he left off. He rides a three-fight winning streak into his UFC Fight Night 283 main event Saturday vs. home country welterweight Uros Medic (13-3 MMA, 7-3 UFC). With great risk comes great reward – but in some regards, the battle is already won.

"Just getting here to this point is a victory in its own," Rodriguez said. "Being able to come out here and headline a UFC fight, see my face on billboards, and just feeling the respect is unbelievable, man. It's truly a dream come true. There were times where I'd pray for this, just to be able to still do this. Getting out and the story blowing up like it did and the UFC giving me a new contract and this opportunity and a tough opponent, it definitely made me rise to the occasion and embrace it in this moment.

"Coming out with a victory will definitely be historic, not only for me but for the whole MMA community and all of Los Angeles and everybody that's rocking with me and all the fans and my family. Everybody knows what I've been through and how hard I've worked to get here to this moment right now. It's an amazing story. I feel like it's definitely a story that needs to be in a movie."

title: Delta-8, THC products come off Texas shelves Friday under new state ban
description: Starting Friday, Texas health officials are reclassifying Delta-8, Delta-10 and other THC isomers as controlled substances. Here's what to know.
fullText:
The deadline for various Delta-8 and THC products is here, as the products will be leaving shelves in Texas on Friday.

Starting July 31, the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) is set to reclassify Delta-8 THC and several other hemp-derived THC isomers — that are not delta-9 THC — as controlled substances in the state.

DSHS adopted new definitions for "Tetrahydrocannabinols" (THC) and "Marihuana Extract," with the change affecting products containing cannabinoids such as Delta-8, Delta-10, Delta-, and THCP, which was published in a July 10 public notice in the Texas Register.

In a July 27 social media post, the Texas Hemp Business Council said businesses cannot sell these products after July 31 and advised them to evaluate their inventory and prepare to remove or sell through products containing more than trace amounts of cannabinoids that fall within the reinstated definition.

Short answer: no under state and federal law.

However, Texas does allow medical use of low-THC cannabis through the state's Compassionate Use Program.

Products like delta-8 and THCA flower can create effects strikingly similar to those of delta-9 THC — the main intoxicating compound in cannabis, often called weed — which is illegal in Texas.

The key difference is how they're made and how they behave.

Delta-8 is a modified form of THC found in small amounts in hemp and usually converted from other cannabinoids. It can produce intoxicating or psychoactive effects, but it is not the same compound as Delta-9 THC.

THCA is sold as raw hemp flower and isn't intoxicating on its own.

But when it's heated — like by smoking or vaping — it turns into delta-9 THC, the same compound found in cannabis.

title: NATO member Romania shoots down stray drones from Ukraine war after years of incursions
description: Since Russia’s full invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the war has repeatedly spilled across Romania's border as drones violate the airspace of the neighboring European Union and NATO member.  Now ...
fullText:
BUCHAREST, Romania (AP) — Since Russia's full invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the war has repeatedly spilled across Romania's border as drones violate the airspace of the neighboring European Union and NATO member.

Now Romania is trying something new to stop the incursions: shooting down the drones.

Romanian pilots shot down the first of three drones in as many days from F-16 fighter jets starting Friday as Russia intensified attacks against Ukraine near the border. After determining the drones were of Russian origin, Romania summoned Moscow's ambassador in protest and expelled a Russian diplomat on Monday.

Drones have crossed into Romanian territory multiple times from Ukraine to the north and east, including in May when a drone injured a mother and child after crashing into an apartment block in the eastern town of Galati along the Danube River.

Romanian authorities largely responded by scrambling jets, collecting debris, erecting fallout shelters near the border and frequently admonishing Moscow for its war spilling into its territory.

Romania and Poland also acquired the MEROPS system, which fires short counter-drones to take down incoming stray drones, following a spate of incursions along NATO's eastern flank late last year.

Drones have crossed into the territories of multiple EU countries, but have been a persistent problem for Romania's leadership in the capital Bucharest. At least 19 have entered Romania's airspace this year, while there have been 50 cases of drones or drone fragments identified on its territory since the war started in 2022, according to Romania's Ministry of National Defense.

Romanian President Nicusor Dan on Sunday congratulated the Romanian pilots for downing the drones and blamed Russia for the incursions.

"It is unacceptable and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romanian airspace," he said.

Despite passing legislation last year to shoot down drones in its airspace, which was strongly opposed by nationalist political parties, Romania has avoided shooting them down until now.

Romanian military analyst Radu Tudor said the May drone incident in Galati may have "changed something in the Romanian authorities' mentality" in how to approach the issue.

"This was somehow a kind of psychological trigger, in order to say: 'OK, enough is enough,'" Tudor said. "Until now, it probably was an Allied decision in NATO not to respond with firepower, because it was somehow a danger of escalation."

"I think it's not only a change of attitude of Romania, I think it's a change of attitude in NATO," he added.

Before the three interceptions over the past week, Romanian pilots also shot down a stray Ukrainian drone above Estonia in May. Romanian pilots and planes are based in Lithuania to provide broad strike capabilities for NATO.

"They saw so many signals that Russia is trying to provoke NATO," Tudor said. "Romania is the only NATO country who shot down four drones on the eastern flank — three on Romania and one in Estonia."

The message sent to Moscow mirrors a statement by NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at the organization's summit in Ankara, Turkey, earlier this month: "'Don't play with us'."

In response to the drone incursions, Romania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Russia's ambassador in Bucharest on Monday and presented him with fragments of a drone, saying Moscow "bears exclusive responsibility for all these grave incidents." The ministry also expelled a member of the Russian mission, who was given five days to leave the country.

"The Russian side learned what they already knew: the drones downed on Romanian territory belong to them," Foreign Minister Oana Toiu wrote in a post on X. "Drone fragments recovered by the Ministry of National Defence and the ongoing prosecutor investigation confirm their Russian origin beyond any doubt."

The Russian embassy in Romania responded in a statement posted on its Facebook page, saying Russia "has never directed and does not direct combat drones" to Romanian territory and denied the allegation as "completely unfounded."

"An unprovoked expulsion of a Russian employee will not go unanswered," the embassy said.

Cristian Popovici, the Romanian defense ministry's head of public relations and a former air defense officer, said tactics have been developed to eliminate errant drones.

"We recorded more than 100 attacks with drones near our border with Ukraine, and many of them resulted in debris or even drones that penetrated our airspace," he told The Associated Press. "Our pilots and our air force, we developed the tactics, procedures, and now we can face and we can eliminate this threat."

The change began when Romanian pilots shot down a drone over Estonian airspace and from that point the military applied "lessons learned" and had a "100% rate success in three days with three drones," Popovici said.

Despite the new approach to stray drones, Popovici said Romania does not plan to become entangled in the war between Russia and Ukraine.

"We are in a peacetime, we are not involved in this fight," he said. "If Russia wants to escalate with NATO, it's up to them. I'm not sure it's a wise move now."

McGrath reported from Leamington Spa, England.

title: Blanche nomination uncertain as key GOP senator says DOJ ‘radio silent’ on demand to spike controversial fund
description: The fate of Todd Blanche’s nomination to be President Donald Trump’s attorney general is up in the air, with a key GOP senator indicating Tuesday he has not yet received the assurances he needs to vot...
fullText:
The fate of Todd Blanche's nomination to be President Donald Trump's attorney general is up in the air, with a key GOP senator indicating Tuesday he has not yet received the assurances he needs to vote in support.

Sen. John Cornyn said around midday Tuesday that he hadn't received an update from the Justice Department on his and Sen. Thom Tillis' demand that the "anti-weaponization" fund be formally killed before they vote in favor of advancing Blanche's nomination.

Later, Cornyn told CNN he would meet with Blanche on Wednesday morning, and he expected the Justice Department to provide a written proposal on how it plans to kill the controversial fund once and for all.

"We need paper. We need it in writing. We don't need well wishes or, you know, impressions," Cornyn said.

Both Cornyn and Tillis, a North Carolina Republican, sit on the Senate Judiciary Committee, which is scheduled to vote Thursday morning on whether to move forward on Blanche's nomination. Without the backing of both lawmakers, the vote will fail.

"They've been kind of radio silent for the last 24 hours," Cornyn said of the DOJ. "I think my staff is talking to them, but we're not — they know what they need to do. They just don't want to do it."

Tillis, though, signaled optimism that the Trump administration would ultimately make an agreement with lawmakers, telling CNN's Manu Raju that talks on the issue are "going pretty well." He said he was unsure if he would go to the Wednesday meeting with Cornyn.

"Hopefully, we can get the White House to execute" on fully killing the fund, Tillis said.

"I think me and Cornyn are of the mind this has to be done," he added.

Blanche has insisted that the "anti-weaponization" fund — a controversial pool of money set aside to award people who claim to have been wronged by the Justice Department, including possibly January 6, 2021, rioters — is no longer happening.

At a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing earlier this month, the acting attorney general insisted bluntly that "the weaponization fund is dead," and said that the tax addendum — which is the only part of the agreement between Trump's personal attorneys and the Justice Department that still stands — "binds only the IRS and by extension the Treasury" from investigating the president for potential crimes, not other agencies. The administration had also previously asserted in a court filing that it had abandoned the "anti-weaponization" fund.

But the two GOP senators have sought more assurances, including a written adjustment to the settlement agreement.

On Tuesday around midday, Cornyn raised the possibility of postponing the committee vote until the issue of the fund is sorted out. "That's being discussed. That's being discussed, but hopefully it won't be necessary," the Texas Republican said, though he noted that he hasn't discussed the idea with Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley yet.

The $1.8 billion fund has been controversial from the start, upending other Senate priorities as critics said it amounted to a slush fund to allow the president to pay out his supporters with taxpayer money. And even while the administration sought to convince lawmakers it was dead, Trump had refused himself to do so, exacerbating tensions on Capitol Hill.

Last week, Cornyn had said that he didn't expect Grassley to postpone the vote. However, as the vote gets closer, that may change.

If the votes aren't there to confirm him, Cornyn said Thursday, "then Sen. Grassley might decide to postpone it. But that's not — I don't think that's the number one goal right now."

Asked later if he would vote against Blanche at the Thursday committee meeting if the weaponization fund issue wasn't resolved to his satisfaction, Cornyn said: "Well, that means I doubt we have the vote." Grassley ignored questions Tuesday about whether he would delay the Thursday vote.

title: Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband details ‘big spiral’ as expert says one part ‘scared me’ in mom’s murder trial
description: Patrick Clancy testified about his ex-wife's mental health spiral on Seroquel and her intrusive thoughts about harming their children before the killings.
fullText:

Patrick Clancy, the father of three young children strangled inside their Massachusetts home, became the first witness Monday in his ex-wife's murder trial, offering jurors a harrowing account of the mental health decline he witnessed before their deaths.

He was the first witness called in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, who faces murder charges in the deaths of the couple's three children in January 2023. Prosecutors argue she acted deliberately, while defense attorneys contend severe mental illness drove her actions.

Patrick described watching his then-wife fall into a "big spiral" after she began taking Seroquel, testifying that she lost weight, became severely depressed and began expressing suicidal thoughts.

"Awful," he said when asked how Lindsay was doing physically after starting the medication. "That was really where her big spiral started. She started to lose a lot of weight, and she became very depressed, and she was having a really hard time."

Lindsay Clancy's Husband Could Testify For Her At Trial Over Deaths Of Their Three Children

Patrick also testified that Lindsay told him she was experiencing intrusive thoughts about harming their children, although she denied having a plan and said the thoughts disturbed her.

"I never saw Lindsay harm the kids," he told jurors.

Margaret McLean, a former criminal prosecutor and trial attorney who teaches law at Boston College's Carroll School of Management, said Patrick's measured delivery did little to conceal the anguish of a father being forced to retrace the months preceding his children's deaths.

"I think his demeanor on the stand is really quite clinical. He's telling it as it is," McLean told Fox News Digital. "You can see the anguish within this man's eyes, his facial expressions. You can tell he's anguished up there, and it's a horrible thing to have to relive and talk about."

McLean said Patrick appeared to be compartmentalizing his emotions as he listened carefully to the questions and provided straightforward answers.

"He's got to get through this," she said. "He's got to listen to the questions and provide the answers as best he can, and I think that he's doing that."

Heated Lindsay Clancy Courtroom Exchange Over 911 Call, Crime Scene Photos Sets Stage For Mom's Murder Trial

Patrick testified that he was not concerned for the children's safety when Lindsay first shared that the intrusive thoughts were telling her to hurt herself as well as her children. Moments after discussing the thoughts, he said, she could be seen making the children lunch, playing with them or preparing them for bed.

Patrick told jurors that he became alarmed after Lindsay was prescribed 13 psychiatric medications in the months prior to the murders and that he pushed for an in-person appointment because he believed there was a "disconnect" between the seriousness of her condition and the brief telehealth sessions she was receiving.

"It seemed like most of her telehealth appointments were pretty quick, and there just wasn't, like, a lot of attention," he said.

Patrick also described taking Lindsay to hospital emergency departments and helping her enter McLean Hospital after she continued expressing suicidal thoughts.

He testified that he "would have paid anything" if insurance had become an obstacle to keeping her hospitalized.

The testimony could leave jurors asking whether the warning prompted an adequate response, McLean said, while cautioning against placing blame on Patrick or family members who may not have understood the severity of the risk.

"So many people don't understand mental health today, so I'm not blaming him at all," McLean said. "Anybody might have done what he did, but that's the part that scared me."

WATCH: Lindsay Clancy clutches tissues as jurors hear about her three children

Patrick's testimony followed starkly different opening statements from prosecutors and the defense.

Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham told jurors that Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, were "deliberately and meticulously killed" by their mother on Jan. 24, 2023.

Buckingham alleged that Clancy deliberately sent Patrick from their Duxbury home to pick up medication and takeout food, giving herself enough time to strangle each child with an exercise band before attempting to kill herself.

McLean said Buckingham gave jurors a "roadmap of cold, calculated intent" while humanizing each child's interests and focusing on the time and physical effort required to carry out three separate strangulations.

"The prosecution did that because she [Buckingham] wants the jury to remember that the act of strangulation takes time and physical effort," McLean said. "It requires a conscious choice to continue three separate times."

The Commonwealth's strategy, she said, is to reject the defense's bid that Clancy suffered a sudden psychotic break and instead portray her as organized, purposeful and controlled.

During opening statements, defense attorney Kevin Reddington conceded that Clancy killed the children but argued that the only meaningful dispute is what was happening inside her mind.

"She knows that she killed these children," Reddington told jurors. "The issue for consideration is what was going on in that woman's mind."

McLean described the concession as a calculated move by a veteran trial attorney.

"By doing that, he is attempting to strip the prosecution of their shock value and force the jury to look purely at Lindsay Clancy's mental capacity," she said.

Reddington argued that Clancy had no motive to kill children she had loved and nurtured. He also displayed graphic hospital photographs showing Clancy with injuries to her neck and wrists.

McLean said the defense was framing Clancy's paralysis "not as a consequence of a crime, but as the tragic final symptom of a complete postpartum psychotic break."

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital, has pleaded not guilty to three counts each of murder and strangulation. Her attorneys do not dispute that she killed the children but argue that she lacked criminal responsibility because of severe postpartum psychosis.

Judge William Sullivan told jurors that the Commonwealth must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Clancy was criminally responsible when the children were killed.

The show's new executive producer, Nick Bilton, announced the news in a staff memo Tuesday, shared on X. Joining Douthat and O'Donnell will be author Sebastian Junger, Trevor Phillips and Gianna Toboni. All will be contributors to the show.

The new journalists join current correspondents Lesley Stahl, Jon Wertheim and Bill Whitaker. Their hirings come two months after a shakeup at the storied program, led by the network's new editor-in-chief, Bari Weiss.

Weiss installed Bilton, who has little substantive broadcast news experience, as executive producer, replacing Tanya Simon, who was let go after a 30-plus year tenure with the show. Also let go were correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega — and soon after, Scott Pelley, after a tense confrontation with his bosses over the changes.

In addition to the three dismissed, Anderson Cooper — whose primary job is at CNN — said earlier this year he was leaving of his own accord after two decades.

Weiss and Tom Cibrowski, the CBS News president, praised the new hires in an internal memo. "We couldn't be more excited about this news," the two said, welcoming the new additions. "Onward!"

Bilton called Douthat "one of the preeminent public intellectuals in America today, a thinker of uncommon rigor and a journalist of deep empathy." The columnist has spent nearly two decades at the Times and is an author of numerous books.

The producer called O'Donnell "a powerhouse."

"You've seen her all over the network. She's launched a new podcast. And you'll see much more of her in our halls because Norah will be a correspondent on 60 Minutes."

Bilton praised Junger for his nonfiction work "The Perfect Storm," about a catastrophic 1991 storm. The book "landed with an electric charge in the world of reported nonfiction, defining an intense and intimate form of storytelling and establishing Sebastian as a generational talent," Bilton said.

Toboni joins"60 Minutes" as a contributor and CBS News as a national correspondent. Previously a senior correspondent with VICE News and VICE on HBO, she comes to the program from CNN.

Calling her a journalist of "extraordinary range," Bilton noted that Toboni has interviewed members of ISIS, investigated cartel violence in Mexico and has written a book on the death penalty.

Also serving as contributor will be Trevor Phillips, announced last month as the news division's senior global affairs correspondent. Based in London, he is "one of the most respected and trusted voices in the United Kingdom for his ability to ask the toughest questions and hold anyone in power to account," Bilton wrote in his memo.

Turmoil had raged at "60 Minutes" for more than a year before the May shakeup. Much of it came after President Donald Trump sued the show over its editing of a 2024 interview with then-Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris.

That became part of a broader shakeup at CBS News after Weiss was named to the new role of editor-in-chief by parent company Paramount late last year following David Ellison's arrival as the network's corporate leader.

Jocelyn Noveck covers the intersection of media and entertainment for The Associated Press.

title: Newly released Biden audio recordings include references to ‘classified’ material and struggles with memory
description: Audio clips released by the right-wing Oversight Project on Monday of former-President Joe Biden’s conversations with his biographer, Mark Lewis Zwonitzer, appears to support what former Special Couns...
fullText:
Audio clips released by the right-wing Oversight Project on Monday of former-President Joe Biden's conversations with his biographer, Mark Lewis Zwonitzer, appears to support what former Special Counsel Robert Hur found in his 2024 report: Biden disclosed classified material, was forgetful and continued to possess classified material after leaving his post as vice president.

In the audio tapes, Biden can be heard cavalierly discussing the notes he kept from his time as vice president as he showed them to Zwonitzer.

"They didn't even know I had this," Biden said while apparently showing the ghostwriter his old notes as reference points in their discussion of allegedly classified foreign policy matters during his VP days. The information is still redacted in the audio clips.

The tapes were released by the Oversight Project, a branch of the conservative think-tank powerhouse Heritage Foundation, who had successfully sued the Justice Department to release them. Biden had fought the release to no avail, ultimately deciding to give up the battle by withdrawing his legal challenges on Monday.

A representative for Biden declined to comment specifically on the release of the audio clips Monday, but spokesperson TJ Ducklo said in a statement last week: "President Biden's conversations for a book a decade ago that discussed his late son are private, and were provided to the Department of Justice on the express condition they stay that way. Reversing course and making them public is just the latest example of this Administration weaponizing the DOJ for political retribution."

In multiple instances in the audio tapes, Biden stumbles in remembering dates and information during the interviews with his ghostwriter, and leaves some thoughts unfinished.

In one instance, while discussing apparently sensitive information that has been blacked out in transcripts of the interviews and muted in audio clips, Biden appears to forget what he was going to ask, adding "oh gosh. I, I can't think of what it is."

When he is seemingly reminded of the subject at hand, Biden warns his ghostwriter, "some of this may be classified, so be careful."

At other times, Biden points to others who might have information about the topic being discussed.

While trying to recall the name of an economic advisor, Biden says, "I should write the names down because I keep forgetting them."

In the Hur report, Biden is described as an elderly man "with a poor memory."

Hur ultimately decided not to bring a case against Biden in part because of his cooperation, which supported the notion that he had not intentionally broken the law but instead did so mistakenly. But Biden's memory and age also weighed into the decision and how a jury might respond to such prosecution.

"Since March 2024, the Oversight Project and the Heritage Foundation fought tooth and nail to bring these tapes to light," the group said in a statement on Monday. "Together, we defeated both the Biden-led Justice Department and his high-price private attorneys. These tapes we are releasing today should have come out a long time ago."

Biden, in one of the released audio clips, said to his ghostwriter that he had "just found" classified documents and then proceeded to lay out his case for why in 2009 he argued against then-President Barack Obama sending troops to Afghanistan.

"So this was – I, early on, in '09 – I just found all of the classified stuff downstairs. I wrote the President a handwritten 40-page memorandum arguing against deploying additional troops to Iraq – I mean, to Afghanistan on the grounds that it wouldn't matter, that the day we left would be like the day before we arrived" Biden said.

In another interview with the ghostwriter, Biden referred to classified information, but the context was unclear.

"And then — and then the next thing I have here is — this is classified," Biden said.

Biden said former President Barack Obama used to really "get pissed" at him over disagreements on how to handle the economy in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis.

"I was a really lonely voice on housing, I was a lonely voice on the middle class. I mean, I thought we should be much more aggressive than putting these guys in jail and the bankers," he said. "I mean, he used to really get pissed at me," he added, referring to Obama.

He said the reason the administration did not do more was because Obama and his allies were "subconsciously" beholden to "Silicon Valley."

"I think the reason why we didn't do more, by the way, is because I think that — this is a harsh thing to say — But I think subconsciously, at least, Barack and his guys were beholden to Silicon Valley," he said. "And the valley guys didn't want the shit that I — you know, I wanted," he said.

Biden also said that Obama backed away from a "promise" to appoint Larry Summers to the Federal Reserve because the prominent economist was a "liability."

"He was, you know, Harvard and women," Biden told Zwonitzer. Summers, who once served as Treasury secretary under President Bill Clinton and as president of Harvard University, has caught backlash over his ties to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Biden said that one thing he wasn't focused on while the administration was trying to save the economy was "how rapidly the economy was changing."

"I wasn't focused on robots and artificial intelligence and, and digitalization and Moore's law. I mean, it was all about — and I really believed that, and I still believe it, that we could bring back the manufacturing in America," he said.

The tapes also included a several-minutes-long recollection from Biden of a lunch meeting with Obama, where Biden said the then-president gave him advice about whether he should run for president in 2016.

"He said it's my decision to run or not. It doesn't have to do with the field," Biden recalled.

Biden indicated that Obama questioned whether his vice president could win the nomination over Hillary Clinton, saying that it would "really be an uphill battle," according to Biden.

"The fact is that he didn't think it was doable at that time, that I could, that I could actually go out and get the nomination," Biden said. "That was my read at the time."

It's not clear from the recording when the meeting between Biden and Obama took place, though Biden provided the details to his ghostwriter just days before the 2016 election, on November 3, 2016.

Biden talked to the ghostwriter about various meetings he had with top advisors strategizing about whether he should announce a run for president, how he should frame his candidacy and when he should announce. In the audio recording, Biden does not specify the year the meetings took place.

"Consensus is that it's no longer a question about is the race doable, it is, the question was when would I need to show my hand to be plausible, he said.

In another meeting, Biden recalled one of his advisers telling him, "you have the ability to be a unifier, a reassuring skill. Hillary is divisive and Bernie is too angry."

Biden also discussed with aides what some of his challenges as a candidate would be and one mentioned his gaffes as one of the many obstacles he would have to overcome.

"Gaffe issue, is like a virus. It's dormant, when you make a mistake again they'll bring it up," Biden said, appearing to be reading from his notes.

"I can't read my own writing" the former president said at one point.

This headline and story have been updated with additional details.

title: ‘He’s bored’: Banfield has theory on Kohberger plea reversal push

fullText:
(NewsNation) — A year after pleading guilty to the murders of four University of Idaho students, Bryan Kohberger is challenging his conviction.

According to a handwritten post-conviction petition, the criminology student claims he was "convinced to falsely confess" to the crimes. He claims he was swayed into the plea deal that landed him life in prison through "coercion, disinformation, false promises, and the withholding of exculpatory discovery."

While Kohberger claims he had ineffective counsel who "misrepresented" what life in prison would be like, NewsNation contributor Ashleigh Banfield told Hena Doba on Monday she believes Kohberger's just bored.

"Life in prison is really awful," she said. "And when you're his age, you're facing about 70 years of this last one year that he's had. He didn't like his last year. He's been in solitary. It's boring. He's tired of it."

Banfield also believes it's not just prison life getting him down, but that Kohberger misses the spotlight he had during his trial.

"He's got a massive ego, and he wants to be relevant again, and he wants to be heard."

As for his claim that his attorneys coerced him into pleading guilty to the murders of Madison Mogen, Xana Kernodle, Ethan Chapin, and Kaylee Goncalves in November 2022 — Banfield doesn't believe that for a second.

"This is a criminology student who was in a Ph.D. program and who intelligently, according to the judge's own words, made them freely and voluntarily in court," Banfield said. "You do have the right to appeal when you think your attorney may have screwed you. The truth is, Anne Taylor could not be a better attorney. She saved that man's life."

Banfield noted that if a judge decides to look into reversing his guilty plea, Kohberger would need a robust argument to prove his attorney was ineffective or withheld evidence that could have proven his innocence.

"You can't just say, 'I was cheated. I didn't get it.' You can't do that," she said. "And I don't believe for an instant that there's some magical discovery that was somehow suppressed from his view."

fullText:
The mysterious death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells has taken another turn after a newly obtained document listed the missing teen's alcohol intake as "heavy" as authorities searched for him on Horn Island over the Fourth of July weekend.

The document, a July 5 Mississippi Department of Marine Resources Marine Patrol email obtained by Fox News Digital, was sent to the U.S. Coast Guard as authorities searched for Wells.

Along with his physical description and last known location, the email lists "Alcohol intake: Heavy," but does not identify the source of that information.

Wells disappeared while on a boating trip to Horn Island with friends. An extensive multi-agency search ended July 6 when his body was discovered.

Search Called Off After Body Matching Missing Teen Nolan Wells Found Off Mississippi Coast

Authorities have not publicly identified a cause or manner of death, and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy and toxicology results remain pending.

The newly reported details come days after a private autopsy commissioned by Wells' family concluded his cause and manner of death were "undetermined pending investigation."

Nolan Wells Independent Autopsy Doesn't Point To Foul Play, Former Medical Examiner Says

During a July 22 news conference, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said an area of "red discoloration" was found on the back of Wells' head but said Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed the independent autopsy, could not determine a cause or manner of death pending further investigation.

"Crime Stories with Nancy Grace" host Nancy Grace later discussed the findings on her show, where she raised additional questions about the investigation.

She pointed to what she described as deep red tissue beneath the skin at the back of Wells' head and said the independent pathologist did not receive Wells' lungs or throat when conducting the second autopsy.

Grace also questioned whether those findings could be significant but emphasized that she did not know what caused Wells' death and noted there were "many accidental possibilities."

"There is deep, red, subcutaneous tissue" on the back of Wells' head, Grace said, adding that the discoloration was localized rather than consistent with postmortem blood pooling.

"I don't know," Grace said. "There are many accidental possibilities."

The Jackson County District Attorney has defended the investigation amid growing public scrutiny, saying authorities are following standard procedures and awaiting forensic testing before drawing conclusions.

Authorities have not announced whether foul play is suspected.

title: Cyclospora outbreak may involve more than lettuce, former CDC lead says
description: Robert Redfield told "Elizabeth Vargas Reports" there's a risk to the public right now with fresh produce and where it's purchased.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — The cyclospora outbreak continues to be a point of concern for health professionals, with one former CDC director saying people should now be cautious about more than just lettuce.

Michigan health officials noted Monday there are 9,253 cases in the state and 160 residents were hospitalized as of last week. The disease has been linked to other states in the Midwest, with a record number of cases being reported.

The CDC has documented more than 4,000 laboratory-confirmed cases, and state records suggest the total number of cases has increased to nearly 12,000.

Recently, a second separate cyclospora outbreak, with no known origin, has sickened 72 people as of last week.

Robert Redfield told "Elizabeth Vargas Reports" there's a risk to the public right now with fresh produce and where it's purchased. He specifically pointed out internationally sourced produce as an issue.

"If you look historically at the outbreaks we've had in the United States, they've really come from produce that was sourced outside of the continental United States," he said.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration linked the first outbreak to distributor Taylor Farms, which sources its lettuce from central Mexico.

Taylor Farms also voluntarily recalled products distributed across 27 states and sold to Taco Bell. Officials have added they believe parsley and cilantro are linked to the outbreak, along with lettuce.

Redfield notes it's a good thing the recalls are occurring.

"I think there have been some serious attempts to stop sourcing from central Mexico right now," he added.

Redfield expanded on the sources of the outbreak, agreeing with Scott Gottlieb, the former commissioner of the FDA, that there's one yet to be identified.

Gottlieb acknowledged he doesn't feel the outbreak is fully under control because there are questions about possible regions besides central Mexico responsible for the issue.

The Hill contributed to this report.

The 2026-27 Prem final will be held on Saturday, 19 June 2027 at the Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, with the season to take a series of breaks around international fixtures.

After five rounds in six weeks through September and October, there will be a four-week Prem break through November for the autumn matches of the Nations Championship.

With European competition beginning in December there are four Prem rounds across six weeks until January, before a 10-week league pause again in February and March for the Six Nations.

The new season also begins with promotion and relegation officially scrapped from the division.

While no club has been relegated from the Prem or promoted up from the Champ since Saracens in 2020 and 2021, this has now been formalised as part of a series of changes to English rugby voted through in February, as the league moves towards a franchise-style model.

title: Jersey's Nowacki makes history with Commonwealth gold
description: Filip Nowacki becomes the most decorated Jersey athlete in Commonwealth Games history after winning gold in the 200m breaststroke.
fullText:
Filip Nowacki has become the most decorated Jersey athlete in Commonwealth Games history after winning gold in the 200m breaststroke.

The 18-year-old, who won 100m breaststroke silver on Saturday, becomes only the second person from the island to win a gold medal.

It comes as the world junior and British senior champion looks to take over the mantle from 50m and 100m world record-holder and former Olympic champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty.

Nowacki, who has beaten some of Ramsay-Peaty's British junior records, finished ahead of the 2016 and 2020 Olympic champion in the 100m breaststroke final.

The Jerseyman also pushed Ramsay-Peaty all the way in the 50m final, finishing fifth behind the Englishman who won bronze.

Nowacki led from start to finish as he opened up a 0.72 second lead after 150m before coming home in a time of 2:07.87, beating Canada's Oliver Dawson into second place with Australia's Zac Stubblety-Cook winning bronze.

Nowacki's success has secured Jersey's first gold since Colin Mallett topped the podium in fullbore shooting in 1990.

But in a winning a gold and silver he has surpassed Mallett's feat in Auckland when he also won fullbore pairs bronze with his father Cliff.

Nowacki wins Jersey's first medal in 36 years

Is struggling Ramsay-Peaty nearing the end?

"It's absolutely unreal," Nowacki told BBC Jersey after the victory.

"People don't understand that you just enter such a heavy flow state during the race, and all of a sudden you finish and you pop back into reality and the crowd comes in."

He added: "It's very special and I owe it to two groups of people.

"My family being my main support and my girlfriend, and also I think the big thing in English swimming is coaches often don't get along between boarding school and club coaches, so the second group of people I put that down to is my coaches."

Nowacki has just left Millfield School and will move to Loughborough to continue his training as he aims towards the 2028 Olympic Games.

He won two world junior titles last year, including the 200m breaststroke, and says he is happy with how he has adapted to the senior environment.

"That jump between junior and senior is huge and it's often overlooked.

"So I'm very pleased to have got my hand on the wall first.

"You don't often see swimmers make that jump straight away, so I'm very fortunate and grateful to have made that jump."

The impact of Nowacki's achievement on his home island of Jersey should not be underestimated.

Competitors representing the Channel Island with a population of about 100,000 had won just four medals before these games.

Nowacki has increased that tally by 50% and become the first-ever swimmer from the island to win a medal.

"There'll be children watching tonight that will want to be like Filip, so it means everything to all of the team here and all of those people watching back home," Jersey's chef de mission Jean Cross told BBC Jersey.

"I think we'll see Filip in LA [for the Olympics], there's so many people talking about Filip here and it's just lovely to be associated with a swimmer of his talent

"He's a true ambassador for Jersey, he's done so well."

Nowacki's victories propel him to one of Jersey's greatest ever sports stars.

The Commonwealth Games is the highest level at which athletes from the island, with a population of about 100,000, can compete under their own flag.

Previous to Colin and Cliff Mallett, Jersey had won just two medals in their own right.

In 1986, bantamweight boxer John Sillitoe won bronze in Edinburgh, while Jersey's first-ever medal was also in the ring when Albert Turmel won welterweight bronze in Perth in 1962.

Islanders have won medals for England - diver Dot Macready won 10m gold in 1934, while more recently Serena Guthrie was part of the England team that won netball gold in 2018.

In 2006, Rebecca Herbert was part of the England hockey team that won bronze, while there were two bronze medals in 2002 for islanders representing England - Elizabeth Cann in badminton and swimmer Simon Militis in the 200m backstroke.

But with Nowacki aged just 18 and already a British senior and world junior champion few would bet against the swimmer going on to become the most decorated Commonwealth Games athlete in Jersey's history.

He is also part of the Team GB set up with an aim firmly on the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Jersey has not had an Olympic competitor since Militis went to the 2000 Olympics in Sydney and all island eyes will be on their young hero bringing them more glory.

title: O'Connor bounces back to lead O'Dowda in heptathlon
description: Northern Ireland's Kate O'Connor is three events away from a first Commonwealth Games gold medal as she leads the heptathlon after the opening four events in Glasgow.
fullText:
Northern Ireland's Kate O'Connor is three events away from a first Commonwealth Games gold medal as she leads the heptathlon after the opening four events in Glasgow.

In the absence of Katarina Johnson-Thompson, England's Jade O'Dowda is in second place - 49 points down on O'Connor.

After an evening session which took place as rain hammered Scotstoun Stadium, Australia's Mia Scerri is a distant third while England's Niamh Emerson is in medal contention in fourth place.

The heptathlon concludes on Wednesday with the long jump, javelin and 800m.

O'Connor finished second in Birmingham in 2022 behind Johnson-Thompson - who pulled out on the eve of this edition - but is in a strong position heading into the second day of competition.

The withdrawal of the 33-year-old has opened the door for a first new Commonwealth heptathlon champion in eight years, and O'Connor and O'Dowda are the two leading contenders to top the podium.

O'Connor was third in the 100m hurdles behind Canada's Sienna Macdonald and O'Dowda, but took the overall lead with a 1.82m leap in the high jump ahead of the English athlete.

O'Dowda took the lead off O'Connor after the shot put as the Northern Ireland athlete could only land the fifth-best effort in torrential conditions.

But the 25-year-old rallied to dominate her 200m heat with a time of 24.14 seconds - while O'Dowda ran the second-slowest time - to hold a 49-point margin heading into the final three events.

Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith out of Commonwealths

Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games

O'Connor said she had never competed in rain as heavy as the downpour that hit Glasgow on Tuesday evening, and admitted she struggled with the elements in the shot put.

"It just kept slipping out of my hands and when your chalk gets wet, you might as well have dish soap on your hands," world silver medallist O'Connor told BBC Sport.

"I'm gutted with it to be honest and when I talk about it, I feel a bit emotional because I've made it a lot easier for the rest of them to beat me, so I've got to work really hard now."

But O'Connor's performance in the 200m was scintillating, and she mastered the conditions on track to take an overnight lead.

"I went out and I ran really quick in that, I threw the gauntlet down and ran as fast as I could to make it difficult for the rest of the girls," she added.

"If the sun was shining and it was a nice warm day, I would have been gutted with that time because I've been running quick in training.

"But considering it's lashing rain and freezing cold out there and I had 10 minutes to warm up, I am delighted with that performance."

Northern Ireland's Anna McCauley holds sixth place after she won the second heat of the 200m, and is within 39 points of a bronze medal.

Prior to that, McCauley had finished sixth in the hurdles and high jump, and posted the seventh-best distance in the shot put with 12.13m.

title: I turned down Love Island and won silver at the Commonwealth Games
description: Katie Shanahan was offered the chance to appear on the dating show last year - but decided she wanted to inspire a new generation of young swimmers.
fullText:
In another reality, swimmer Katie Shanahan might have been looking for love on her favourite TV show - but instead made a decision that would lead her to a silver medal at the Commonwealth Games.

The 22-year-old told BBC Scotland News she was offered the chance to appear on Love Island last year, the reality dating show where singletons are placed in a Spanish villa.

However Glasgow-born Shanahan turned down the offer of sunshine in Mallorca, choosing instead to focus on her sport at the Tollcross swimming centre.

Last Friday she claimed silver in the 200m breaststroke on the opening night of the Games.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Despite her sporting success, she says would not be averse to a trip to Casa Amor in the future.

"I'm the biggest Love Island fan ever, I've watched every season", she laughed.

"Last year the producers asked me and Abbie Wood [the English swimmer] if we would be interested in doing it.

"I couldn't go on though, because of focusing on the swimming, but who knows in the future? I was a bit tempted but the swimming had to come first."

Love Island, which concluded its 2026 series earlier this week, has aimed to attract a number of athletes to the programme.

Northern Ireland boxers Jon McConnell and Kaci Rock progressed through initial auditions for the show, but then had to drop out to focus on their sport as the Games drew closer.

A number of lower league and non-league footballers have also appeared on the often controversial dating show over the years.

However Shanahan's decision paid off in the pool, and she was seen fighting back tears after securing silver on Friday night.

Having been inspired by seeing Hannah Miley in action at the 2014 Games, Shanahan told BBC Scotland News she hoped future generations might have be likewise inspired by watching her in the pool this time around.

"I've always said that if I can inspire the next generation of athletes coming through, then my job has been done," she explained.

"I know after 2014 watching Hannah I felt inspired, and it would be nice to think that maybe there's some younger girls watching the 200m backstroke this time, and maybe they'll get into swimming from it."

She joked that the main problem since last Friday was finding the time to get back to various friends and well-wishers sending her messages to congratulate her.

"I'm so grateful for the support, and with it being a home Games it feels like that support has been ramped up a bit, which is so nice to experience."

title: Crawley and Brook help Sunrisers beat Super Giants
description: Leeds Sunrisers end Manchester Super Giants' unbeaten start to the season after chasing down 182 thanks to half-centuries from Mitch Marsh and Zak Crawley while Harry Brook chips in with 42.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Headingley

Manchester Super Giants 181-3 (100 balls): Buttler 63* (33), Klaasen 53 (27); Ellis 2-32

Sunrisers Leeds 186-2 (88 balls): Marsh 63 (26), Crawley 56* (34), Brook 42* (17)

Sunrisers Leeds won by eight wickets

Mitch Marsh was at his destructive best as he bludgeoned 63 to help Sunrisers Leeds end Manchester Super Giants' unbeaten start to The Hundred with an eight-wicket win at Headingley.

The experienced Australia opener crashed six fours and five sixes during a fearless 26-ball knock which provided the impetus for the Sunrisers to chase down 182 for victory.

Marsh was bowled by a yorker from Sonny Baker with the score on 118 but the momentum from his tone-setting innings was continued by England duo Zak Crawley and Harry Brook.

Sunrisers skipper Crawley blitzed an unbeaten 56 off 34 balls to notch only his second half-century of the summer, having lost his Test place earlier this year.

Crawley's average in The Hundred (34.50) so far this summer has been superior to what he has managed in the T20 Blast (23.54) and in first-class cricket (20.54).

The 28-year-old felt "in the zone" and was able to play with "a lot of freedom" as he helped his side pull off the highest successful run chase at Headingley in The Hundred.

"I've spent too much of my career trying to prove to people how I can play. I'm buzzing that I've scored some runs, that's what I get joy out of," Crawley told BBC Test Match Special.

"I'm just thankful I can do that, I'm not too worried about who liked it and who didn't - I know I did and that's what I want to do."

Brook chipped in with 42 not out from 17 balls as he also kickstarted his tournament with an innings bristling with clean ball striking.

The England limited-overs skipper had only managed scores of three and eight in his first two innings but mainly dealt in sixes against the Super Giants.

Brook's six boundaries all cleared the ropes, including the winning runs off Noor Ahmad with 12 balls to spare.

Earlier, England wicketkeeper Jos Buttler continued his impressive start to this year's tournament with an unbeaten 63 off 33 balls which provided the bedrock of the Super Giants' 181-3.

Buttler had made a masterful 90 in the Super Giants' emphatic win over Birmingham Phoenix last weekend and followed it up with his second half-century.

Heinrich Klaasen had chipped with 53 off 27 balls while Aussie seamer Nathan Ellis bagged 2-30 to finish the pick of the Sunrisers' bowlers.

The Sunrisers have won two of their opening matches in The Hundred and join the Super Giants, who stay top on net run-rate, Welsh Fire and MI London on eight points.

The Hundred continues on Wednesday with double-headers in Cardiff and London.

At Sophia Gardens, Welsh Fire's women face Trent Rockets at 11:30 BST before the men's sides meet at 15:00 BST, with both home teams aiming to build on positive starts to the campaign.
